Once the System Menu is running, it uses DIP to detect discs and read Disc Channel data.

items.title: Certificate identity
items.text:
read_certificate_identity (0xFFFF1E20) reads the MS identifier, CA identifier, NG key identifier and NG certificate signature from SEEPROM when OTP keys are present. It formats the issuer components as MS%08x and CA%08x.

read_device_id (0xFFFF1CE0) reads OTP word 9 for the device identifier. The certificate name is formatted as NG%08x using this value. These kernel addresses refer to IOS80.

items.title: Signature verification
items.text:
IOS80's verify_rsa_sha1 (0x13A75514) imports the signature, public modulus and exponent as big integers. It computes signature^exponent mod modulus in software through bigint_power_modulo (0x13A77A40), using multiplication and division for modular reduction. It converts the result back to bytes and checks the signature padding, SHA-1 identifier and supplied 20 byte digest. It returns 0 on success or 7 on failure.

verify_rsa2048 (0x13A75664) selects a 256 byte modulus and verify_rsa4096 (0x13A75680) selects a 512 byte modulus. Disc partition verification uses this path before the partition is marked open.

items.title: Thread waits
items.text:
receive_queued_message (0xFFFF2968) blocks when the queue is empty and its nonblocking argument is zero. It marks the current thread as waiting and yields to the scheduler. After a successful wakeup, it checks the queue again before it reads a message.

Once the service threads are started, the initialization thread lowers its own priority to zero and enters an idle loop at 0xFFFF0C6A. The loop reads g_debug_requests (0xFFFF9ECC) repeatedly while it is zero. When the word is nonzero, the loop passes its value to print_debug_state (0xFFFF6084) to select diagnostic output then clears the word. The loop does not execute a wait-for-interrupt instruction.

Firmware Idle loop g_debug_requests print_debug_state IOS80 v6944 0xFFFF0C6A 0xFFFF9ECC 0xFFFF6084 IOS70 v6687 0xFFFF0C6A 0xFFFF9E8C 0xFFFF6078 IOS35 v3608 0xFFFF0C4C 0xFFFF9BCC 0xFFFF5E24

For an undefined instruction that does not match the syscall encoding, undefined_exception (0xFFFF1F24) saves the exception return address, marks the current thread as faulted with state 6 and calls dispatch_thread (0xFFFF2340). The faulted thread is no longer runnable. The idle loop can therefore run while a service thread is faulted and other services are waiting for messages.

items.title: IPC requests
items.text:
Broadway requests IOS services through shared RAM and the IPC mailboxes. The request in RAM contains a command, a result field and command-specific arguments. The mailbox carries the request's physical address. File paths and transfer buffers are referenced by pointers in the request.

Broadway makes the request visible in RAM before writing its address to the request mailbox and signaling a new request through IPC control. An enabled IPC interrupt notifies Starlet. IOS acknowledges receipt separately from completing the operation, allowing Broadway to submit another request while earlier work remains pending.

IOS dispatches the request to the appropriate service. On completion, it supplies the result in shared RAM and publishes the reply pointer through the return mailbox. Broadway handles the reply interrupt, invalidates the relevant cache lines before reading the result and acknowledges the reply.

items.title: Mailboxes and control flags
items.text:
Broadway physical address Starlet physical address Width Name IOS use 0x0D000000 0x0D800000 32 bits PPCMSG Physical address of a request from Broadway. 0x0D000004 0x0D800004 32 bits PPCCTRL Broadway's handshake flags and interrupt enables. 0x0D000008 0x0D800008 32 bits ARMMSG Physical address of a reply from IOS.

Starlet accesses ARMCTRL at 0x0D80000C. The control registers expose the same four handshake flags at different bit positions:

Flag PPCCTRL bit ARMCTRL bit IOS protocol X1 0 2 Broadway signals a new request. IOS clears it by writing 1 to the ARMCTRL field. X2 3 1 Broadway acknowledges a reply. IOS clears it by writing 1 to the ARMCTRL field. Y1 2 0 IOS signals a reply. Broadway clears it by writing 1 to the PPCCTRL field. Y2 1 3 IOS acknowledges receipt of a request. Broadway clears it by writing 1 to the PPCCTRL field. Register Bit Field Interrupt enable PPCCTRL 4 IY1 Reply notification through Hollywood interrupt 30. PPCCTRL 5 IY2 Request acknowledgement through Hollywood interrupt 30. ARMCTRL 4 IX1 New request through Hollywood interrupt 31. ARMCTRL 5 IX2 Reply acknowledgement through Hollywood interrupt 31.

Writing a mailbox supplies its value. Software signals the corresponding control flag separately. Clearing Y1 consumes the reply notification. Setting X2 tells IOS that it can publish another queued reply.

Broadway sets X1 or X2 by writing 1 to the corresponding PPCCTRL field.

Tip

Writing zero to PPCCTRL clears neither flag!! We tested this on hardware!!

items.title: Startup notification
items.text: On success, set_ipc_access_rights (0xFFFF2ED4) writes 0x38 to ARMCTRL after updating the registered devices' access permissions. This enables IX1 and IX2 and sets Y2, as defined in the control flag tables. The routine does not read a request from PPCMSG or publish a reply through ARMMSG. This startup notification can therefore assert Y2 independently of request receipt.

items.title: IOS reload
items.text:
Broadway requests an IOS reload through /dev/es with IPC command 7 (ioctlv) and ES operation 0x08. The request has two input vectors and no output vectors: an 8 byte title ID and a 0xD8 byte ticket view.

The old IOS acknowledges receipt with Y2 before executing the reload. The input vectors remain in use after this acknowledgement. A successful reload does not return a normal Y1 reply from the old IOS. The new IOS sets Y2 again through its startup notification. These are two separate notifications: request receipt followed by initialization of the new IOS's IPC access rights.

items.title: Request layout
items.text:
The request header occupies 32 bytes. Its words are big endian and buffer pointers are physical addresses.

Byte offset Size Field Meaning 0x00 4 bytes Command Requested IOS operation. 0x04 4 bytes Result Signed result returned by IOS. 0x08 4 bytes Descriptor / original command Input descriptor for operations on an open handle. IOS replaces it with the original command before dispatch. 0x0C 20 bytes Arguments Five command-specific words.

For an open request, command 1 uses a path pointer at 0x0C and a mode at 0x10. IOS checks that the path terminates within 64 bytes. A successful open returns a nonnegative handle. A close request uses command 2 and supplies that handle at 0x08.

items.title: Broadway IPC worker
items.text:
ipc_worker (0xFFFF4ABC) creates a queue with capacity for 50 messages and stores its handle in g_ipc_queue (0xFFFFCE1C). It registers hardware event 31 on that queue with a pointer to g_ipc_event_message (0xFFFFCDFC), whose value is 9. It then waits for queue messages.

Before waiting, the worker reads PPCCTRL. If both IY1 and IY2 are clear, it writes zero to PPCCTRL. If either interrupt enable is set, it leaves PPCCTRL unchanged. The fields are defined in the control flag tables.

rearm_ipc_interrupt (0xFFFF5E2C) clears the IPC interrupt flag and enables its mask. IPC uses bit 31 in HW_ARMIRQFLAG and HW_ARMIRQMASK.

On an IPC interrupt, irq_handler (0xFFFF20D4) clears the IPC mask bit, acknowledges the pending interrupt and calls deliver_event (0xFFFF1FF4) for event 31. Event delivery appends the registered message to its queue and makes a waiting receiver runnable. An unregistered event or a full queue receives no message. Returning from the IRQ handler does not itself unmask IPC.

Register Bits Worker use ARM control (0x0D80000C) 1 Handle Broadway's response acknowledgement. ARM control (0x0D80000C) 2 Read a new Broadway request pointer from 0x0D800000.

For an event message with value 9, the worker checks the control register. It checks response acknowledgement before a new request. When handling a new request, it reads the request pointer, updates the control register and rearms the interrupt before validating and dispatching the request.

If neither X2 nor X1 is set when the worker processes the event message, it returns to waiting for queue messages without rearming the IPC interrupt.

For a new request, it writes the preserved interrupt enables together with 0x0C to ARMCTRL: clear X1 and set Y2. If 47 requests are already pending, it writes 0x04 instead and withholds the receipt acknowledgement for the next request.

Open requests block the worker despite the asynchronous interface. open_async (0xFFFF31D0) calls open_device (0xFFFF3020), which waits for the device service to reply. If another IPC interrupt arrives in the meantime, the IRQ handler masks the source and queues its event. The worker cannot process that event or rearm IPC until the open returns.

queue_ipc_reply (0xFFFF4A0C) places a completed request pointer in a ring with 48 entries. send_ipc_reply (0xFFFF4994) publishes a queued reply only when the reply mailbox is available. It flushes the 32 byte request header, writes the pointer to ARMMSG and sets Y1 through ARMCTRL. It then marks the reply mailbox unavailable until Broadway signals X2.

Publishing a reply reduces the pending request count. When that count is 48 before publication, the control write also sets Y2 to release the withheld receipt acknowledgement. The worker preserves IX1 and IX2 when it writes handshake flags.

items.title: Timer alarm
items.text:
program_alarm (0xFFFF4190) clamps the requested delay to at least two timer ticks. It reads HW_TIMER (0x0D800010) once and saves that sample in g_last_timer_tick (0xFFFFCC14). It adds the delay to the sample with 32 bit wraparound and writes the result to HW_ALARM (0x0D800014).

delay_ticks = max(delay_ticks, 2)
now = HW_TIMER
g_last_timer_tick = now
HW_ALARM = (now + delay_ticks) & 0xFFFFFFFF

items.title: DMA buffer addresses
items.text:
dma_address (0xFFFF52D4) translates a buffer's virtual address through the active page tables and converts SRAM CPU addresses to DMA addresses. The AES and SHA-1 services use the converted address when programming their engines. These addresses refer to IOS80.

SRAM bank CPU physical start CPU physical end (inclusive) DMA start DMA end (inclusive) A 0xFFFF0000 0xFFFFFFFF 0x0D400000 0x0D40FFFF B 0xFFFE0000 0xFFFE7FFF 0x0D410000 0x0D417FFF

The conversion preserves the offset within the bank. MEM1 and MEM2 keep their translated physical addresses.

items.title: AES completion
items.text:
IOS80's AES service thread aes_worker (0x13A7414C) registers event 2 with message value 0 on its completion queue. It submits the AES command with the completion interrupt enabled and waits on that queue.

The kernel IRQ handler acknowledges the AES interrupt by writing 0x00000004 to HW_ARMIRQFLAG (0x0D800038) and then delivers event 2.

items.title: SHA-1 completion
items.text:
IOS80's SHA-1 service thread sha_worker (0x13A74750) registers event 3 with message value 0 on its completion queue. process_sha (0x13A74440) submits whole input blocks with the completion interrupt enabled and waits on that queue. For a single 64 byte block, it writes 0xC0000000 to the SHA-1 control register (0x0D030000).

IOCTLV command 0 requires one input vector and two output vectors. The first output vector supplies the SHA-1 context address. Its declared length is not checked. Operation 0 writes the five SHA-1 initial state words followed by two zero length words to this address even when the input length is zero. A zero length request returns after these 28 bytes are written without starting the SHA-1 engine or writing the digest output vector.

The kernel IRQ handler acknowledges the SHA-1 interrupt by writing 0x00000008 to HW_ARMIRQFLAG (0x0D800038) and then delivers event 3.

items.title: Syscalls
items.text:
Syscalls are undefined ARM instructions. Executing one raises an Undefined Instruction exception and the vector at 0xFFFF0004 jumps to undefined_exception. The handler accepts the instruction word only if every bit outside the index field matches 0xE6000010.

Bits Field Value 31:13 Fixed Same as 0xE6000010 12:5 Index Syscall index 4:0 Fixed Same as 0xE6000010

For example, 0xE6000130 selects index 9. Arguments are passed in r0 through r3 and the result is returned in r0. Execution then resumes at the instruction after the syscall. Indices above 0x7A return immediately with r0 unchanged.

Index Function Arguments Result 0x03 get_thread_id (0xFFFF04A0) None Current thread's index in the kernel thread table 0x08 get_thread_priority (0xFFFF0760) r0 = thread ID (0 selects the current thread) Priority or -4 if the thread ID or process access is rejected 0x09 set_thread_priority (0xFFFF07B0) r0 = thread ID (0 selects the current thread), r1 = priority 0 on success or -4 if the thread or priority is rejected 0x0C send_message (0xFFFF27F8) r0 = queue ID, r1 = message word, r2 = nonblocking flag 0 on success or a negative error 0x0E receive_message (0xFFFF29E4) r0 = queue ID, r1 = writable message-word pointer, r2 = nonblocking flag 0 on success or a negative error 0x15 get_timer (0xFFFF4530) None Current 32 bit HW_TIMER value 0x2A reply_request (0xFFFF408C) r0 = dispatched request pointer, r1 = signed service result Reply delivery result or -4 for a rejected request

The message queue calls accept a nonblocking flag of 0 or 1. With 0, a send to a full queue or a receive from an empty queue suspends the calling thread as described in Thread waits. With 1, the call returns without suspending. Both calls check the queue's owning process. A receive also validates the 4 byte message destination before it accesses the queue.

items.title: DIP
items.text: Firmware behavior and function addresses describe IOS80 unless another IOS version is specified.

items.title: System Menu disc detection
items.text:
The Wii has a slot-loading drive, but the Disc Interface still calls its media state register and related commands "cover". Disc insertion and removal are reported through this interface.

The System Menu accesses the drive through /dev/di. To recognize an inserted disc and show its banner in the Disc Channel, it has to check the media state and read from the disc. For a Wii disc with update and game partitions, System Menu v513 makes these main requests:

  1. Poll the cover register with ioctl 0x7A to detect the disc. Reading the status and acknowledging an interrupt are separate cover commands.
  2. Request drive information with ioctl 0x12 and read the disc ID with ioctl 0x70.
  3. Read disc metadata such as the partition table and region information with the unencrypted read ioctl 0x8D.
  4. Open the update partition with ioctlv 0x8B, read from it with ioctl 0x71 then close it with ioctl 0x8C.
  5. Open the game partition with ioctlv 0x8B and read from it with ioctl 0x71. These reads supply the data the System Menu uses to populate the Disc Channel and show its banner before the user selects Start.

System Menu v513 can perform this detection and partition verification while the health and safety screen is displayed, before the user presses A.

Opening a partition returns its title metadata and makes it the target of subsequent partition reads. These reads must come from the currently open partition, not always from the game partition. Unencrypted reads take offsets relative to the start of the disc while partition reads take offsets into the open partition's decrypted data.

Drive-register initialization and cover interrupt handling are still required, but a cover status response alone does not supply the disc contents the Disc Channel needs.

items.title: Partition verification
items.text:
open_partition (0x20202F34) only works after the disc ID has been read, because that read sets up the encryption and hash flags it uses. It also refuses to open a second partition while one is already open.

Opening a partition reads the partition header, title metadata (TMD) and certificates from the disc. verify_partition (0x20202D14) then passes the ticket, TMD and certificate chain to ES through ioctlv 0x1C, which takes four input vectors and two output vectors:

Vector Direction Contents 0 Input Certificate chain 1 Input Certificate revocation list, empty in this path 2 Input 676 byte ticket 3 Input TMD 4 Output 4 byte key handle 5 Output 20 byte hash for each TMD content

ES reports its result separately from DIP's. A nonzero ES result fails the open. Successful verification is also what sets up the disc's title context in ES, so returning a TMD without going through ES is not enough.

The verification path invokes IOS's software RSA signature verification.

For an encrypted partition, verify_partition_hashes (0x20202BF8) then reads the 0x18000 byte H3 table and checks its SHA-1 digest against the content hashes from ES. The partition is only marked open once this check passes. The partition data address must be aligned to 0x8000 bytes.

items.title: Request dispatch
items.text:
dvd_driver (0x2020062C) registers /dev/di. It passes ioctl arguments to di_ioctl (0x20200400) and vector arguments to di_ioctlv (0x20200284). After the handler returns, the driver passes its result to reply_request (0x20205E88).

Firmware di_ioctl di_ioctlv IOS80 v6944 0x20200400 0x20200284 IOS35 v3608 0x202003B8 0x20200254

Both argument structures begin at byte offset 0x0C in the IOS request. Each field is a 32 bit big endian value, and pointers are addresses in the driver's address space.

Ioctl argument offset Field 0x00 Command 0x04 Input buffer pointer 0x08 Input buffer length in bytes 0x0C Output buffer pointer 0x10 Output buffer length in bytes Ioctlv argument offset Field 0x00 Command 0x04 Input vector count 0x08 Output vector count 0x0C Vector array pointer

Each vector holds a 32 bit buffer pointer followed by a 32 bit length in bytes. Every ioctl except command 0x8E requires a 32 byte input buffer. Command 0x8B opens a partition and must be sent through ioctlv. Sending it through ioctl returns 0x20.

items.title: Cover commands
items.text: Ioctl Operation Result 0x79 Wait for the cover to close. Returns 4 after the wait completes. 0x7A Read DICVR into the first output word. Returns 1 on success or 0x20 if the output is shorter than 4 bytes. 0x85 Disable cover interrupts without acknowledging a pending cover interrupt. Returns 1. 0x86 Acknowledge the cover interrupt. Returns 1. 0x87 Return without accessing the drive. Returns 1. 0x88 Read cover readiness into the first output word. Writes 0 during the first 100 milliseconds of a pending reset, 1 for an open cover or 2 for a closed cover. Returns 1 on success or 0x20 if the output is shorter than 4 bytes. 0x89 Enable cover interrupts without acknowledging a pending cover interrupt. Returns 1.

items.title: Disc cover handling
items.text:
DIP accesses the Disc Interface cover register through virtual address 0x0D006004, mapped to physical address 0x0D806004.

Address Width Firmware access Name Purpose 0x0D006004 32 bits Read/write DICVR Cover state and cover interrupt control

items.title: DICVR - 0x0D006004 (32 bits)
items.text:
Bits Field Firmware use 0 Cover state Require 0 before completing a wait for cover closure. 1 Cover interrupt enable Set before waiting for closure and clear after the wait completes. 2 Cover interrupt status Test when processing an interrupt message and write 1 to acknowledge.

wait_for_cover_close (0x20200B98) enables cover interrupts then waits on its message queue. It ignores messages of type 10 and processes interrupt messages of type 11. A cover interrupt ends the wait only when the reset delay has expired and Cover State is clear. The routine acknowledges the cover interrupt even when those conditions do not allow it to finish.

init_driver_events (0x20200074) registers IOS event 18 with the transaction queue, using a message whose first 32 bit word is 11. Both the cover wait and the drive command completion path receive messages from this queue.

enable_cover_interrupt (0x202009C0) reads DICVR, clears bits 2:1 in the value then sets bit 1 before writing it back. disable_cover_interrupt (0x202009D4) clears bits 2:1 in the read value before writing it back. Both avoid acknowledging an existing cover interrupt as a side effect of changing its enable. acknowledge_cover (0x202009B0) reads the register then writes the value with bit 2 set.

items.title: Status initialization
items.text: init_drive_registers (0x20200D1C) acknowledges any pending transfer-complete and device-error status before enabling the corresponding interrupts. It polls the transfer-complete interrupt enable until the bit reads back as set. It then enables the device-error interrupt and disables the cover interrupt. It also checks that both acknowledged status fields are clear.

items.title: DISR - 0x0D006000 (32 bits)
items.text:
This virtual address maps to physical address 0x0D806000.

Bits Field Firmware use 1 Device-error interrupt enable Set during drive-register initialization. 2 Device-error status Test for a drive error and write 1 to acknowledge it. 3 Transfer-complete interrupt enable Set during drive-register initialization and poll until it reads back set. 4 Transfer-complete status Test for command completion and write 1 to acknowledge it.

clear_device_error (0x20200B80) acknowledges the device error while preserving the interrupt enables.

items.title: Raw disc transfers
items.text:
handle_command (0x20200EF8) programs raw reads through these 32 bit registers, which map to physical 0x0D806008 through 0x0D80601C:

Virtual address Purpose Raw-read value 0x0D006008 Command word 0 0xA8000000 for a raw read or 0xA8000040 for the disc ID 0x0D00600C Command word 1 Disc offset in units of 4 bytes, zero for the disc ID 0x0D006010 Command word 2 Transfer length in bytes 0x0D006014 DMA destination Output buffer address 0x0D006018 DMA length Transfer length in bytes 0x0D00601C Transfer control 3 to start the DMA read

A disc ID read transfers 32 bytes. Raw reads need a 32 byte aligned destination and a length that is a multiple of 32. start_timed_transfer (0x20200E4C) expects the transfer-complete interrupt to be enabled when it writes transfer control. It starts a command timeout timer right after that write.

The driver then waits for messages on its transaction queue. When the transfer-complete interrupt arrives, it stops the timer, acknowledges the status and checks for a device error before reporting success. The data transfer alone does not complete a read. The driver also needs that interrupt message.

items.title: Service startup
items.text:
The EHCI module in IOS58 provides /dev/usb/ehc. ehci_worker (0x138C0E90) creates a 64 message queue and registers the device before calling init_ehci (0x138C1624). It only enters the request loop if initialization succeeds.

If initialization fails, the worker prints ehci_core: EHCI initialization failed followed by ehci_core exits... and stops the thread. The device stays registered, so open requests can still be queued for it even though nothing will ever reply to them.

items.title: Controller initialization
items.text:
The capability registers start at physical address 0x0D040000 and the operational registers at 0x0D040010.

init_ehci requires USBSTS.HCHalted to be set before it requests a controller reset and fails immediately if the bit is clear. It then sets USBCMD.HCRESET, waits two microseconds and checks whether the reset has completed. While the bit stays set it polls up to 100 more times, waiting one microsecond before each read.

Physical address Register Bit Field Firmware use 0x0D040010 USBCMD 1 HCRESET Set to request reset, then polled until clear 0x0D040014 USBSTS 12 HCHalted Must be set before requesting reset

Once the reset completes, the driver requires these exact register values and fails initialization on any mismatch:

Physical address Register Required value 0x0D040010 USBCMD 0x00080000 0x0D040014 USBSTS 0x00001000 0x0D040018 USBINTR 0x00000000 0x0D04001C FRINDEX 0x00000000 0x0D040020 CTRLDSSEGMENT 0x00000000 0x0D040050 CONFIGFLAG 0x00000000

items.title: Schedule control
items.text:
enable_async_schedule (0x138C49B8) and enable_periodic_schedule (0x138C4A24) both go through set_schedule (0x138C48FC). Before changing an enable bit, this helper waits for the matching status bit to agree with the enable bit's current value. It returns -10 if that wait times out. Both wrappers retry until the helper succeeds.

Command register Command bit Status register Status bit Schedule USBCMD 5 USBSTS 15 Asynchronous USBCMD 4 USBSTS 14 Periodic

items.title: Port scan
items.text:
scan_ports (0x138C3448) reads each port's status from 0x0D040050 + 4 * port, with ports numbered from 1. It only runs port change handling for a port when one of these bits is set:

Bits Field 1 Connect status change 3 Port enable change

The scan disables the port change interrupt while it examines the ports. Before returning it acknowledges the pending port change status and enables the interrupt again.

items.title: Startup
items.text:
ncd_main (0x13D901E8) waits 1000 ms before opening /dev/net/wd/command with mode 3. If the open returns -6, it waits 10 ms and tries again. It uses sleep_ms (0x13D962A0), which creates a timer and blocks on a message queue until the timer delivers its message.

sleep_ms(1000);
do {
    handle = open("/dev/net/wd/command", 3);
    if (handle == -6)
        sleep_ms(10);
} while (handle == -6);

items.title: Kernel USB initialization
items.text: Before the OHCI modules initialize their controllers, the kernel's init_usb (0xFFFF6BD8) writes 0xFE, 0xF6, 0xF4, 0xF0, 0x70, 0x60, 0x40 and finally 0x00 to physical address 0x0D800088. Each write is 32 bits wide and followed by a delay.

items.title: OH0 initialization
items.text:
ohci_core (0x138A00AC) initializes the OH0 controller at 0x0D050000. It writes 0x80000000 to 0x0D050014 then reads a 32 bit value from 0x0D050000 and checks its revision field.

Bits Field Required value 7:0 Revision 0x10

If the revision does not match, initialization reports -4 through ohci_core: OHCI initialization failed: %d and takes the exit path before resetting the controller. The comparison ignores the upper 24 bits of the revision register.

items.title: Controller state checks
items.text:
Before requesting a host-controller reset, OH0 reads HcControl at 0x0D050004:

Bits Field Firmware use 7:6 Functional state Must be 0 before requesting reset. 8 Interrupt routing If set, OH0 requests ownership and the bit must then clear.

If either check fails, initialization returns -10. The reset request alone cannot recover a controller left running by an earlier driver instance, so the USB block has to be reset before OH0 starts again.

items.title: Controller reset
items.text:
After the revision and controller-state checks succeed, OH0 requests a reset through 0x0D050008. It uses 32 bit accesses and preserves the other bits when setting the reset request.

Bits Field Firmware use 0 Host controller reset Set to request reset. Wait for the controller to clear it.

OH0 calls delay (0x138A0048) with 10000 microseconds before checking completion. This helper restarts an IOS timer and waits for a message on its completion queue. If the reset request remains set, OH0 waits 2 microseconds between further checks for up to 10000 iterations. A request that remains set after those checks causes initialization to report -10.

items.title: Frame timing
items.text:
After reset completes, OH0 writes 0x27782EDF to HcFmInterval (0x0D050034) using a 32 bit store. TODO: Figure out what the fuck this even does bro

Bits Field Written value Meaning 31 FIT 0 Frame interval toggle 30:16 FSMPS 0x2778 (10104) Initial largest data packet counter value in bits 13:0 FI 0x2EDF (11999) Nominal frame interval encoding at 12 MHz

items.title: OH1 initialization
items.text:
OH1's ohci_core (0x138B008C) uses the controller at 0x0D060000. It calls register_device (0x138B2340) to create a 4 entry request queue and register /dev/usb/oh1 before checking the controller revision.

It writes 0x80000000 to 0x0D060014 then reads 0x0D060000 using 32 bit accesses. The revision must satisfy the same revision-field requirement as OH0. A mismatch reports initialization error -4, frees the controller structure and exits the thread before it enters the request loop.

items.title: Root-hub power delay
items.text:
enumerate_devices (0x138B0934) reads HcRhDescriptorA (0x0D060048) to determine the port count and power delay. After configuring power, it waits POTPGT * 2000 microseconds through an IOS timer before checking the ports.

Bits Field Meaning 7:0 NDP Number of downstream ports. 31:24 POTPGT Power-on delay in units of 2 ms.

items.title: OH1 request dispatch
items.text:
usb_worker (0x138B239C) waits on the registered request queue. Open and close operations return their result through an IOS reply before the worker receives another request.

For device transfer IOCTLV commands 0, 1 and 2, a nonnegative submission result returns the worker to its receive loop without replying to the request. Submission therefore does not itself complete the IPC operation. A negative submission result sends an immediate error reply.

items.title: Transfer lengths
items.text:
submit_endpoint_transfer (0x138B15C0) handles bulk command 1 and interrupt command 2. Both require two input vectors and one output vector.

Vector Size Contents 0 1 byte Endpoint address. 1 2 bytes Transfer length as a big endian unsigned integer. 2 Transfer length Data buffer.

The length in vector 1 must equal the size of vector 2. The endpoint and length pointers must be nonzero. A nonzero transfer length also requires a nonzero data pointer. Invalid vector counts or these validation failures return -4.

Control command 0 uses a different layout. submit_control_transfer (0x138B14B4) requires six input vectors and one output vector. Its transfer length is the LE 16 bit value in vector 4 and must equal the size of the data buffer in vector 6.

items.title: USB Command Format
items.text:
USB commands are sent to the controller as this extremely cursed double nested linked list. Two linked lists are provided in hcctrlhd and hcblkhd, for Control transfers and Bulk transfers respectively.

For both hcctrlhd and hcblkhd, the first level of linked list contains EndpointDescriptors. These are defined as:

Each endpoint descriptor occupies 16 bytes and is aligned to 16 bytes. Its words are little endian, and its pointers refer to physical addresses in guest RAM.

(The fields that are irrelevant for emulation have their descriptions omitted)

Byte offset Size Field Meaning 0x00 4 bytes flags Device address, endpoint number and transfer settings. 0x04 4 bytes tail_pointer Address of the dummy TransferDescriptor marking the end of the queue. 0x08 4 bytes head_pointer Address of the next TransferDescriptor to process, plus endpoint state bits. 0x0C 4 bytes next_endpoint Address of the next EndpointDescriptor. Zero terminates the endpoint list.

The flags word contains:

Bits Field Meaning 6:0 Device address USB address assigned to the device. 10:7 Endpoint number Endpoint on that device. 12:11 Direction 1: OUT. 2: IN. 0 or 3: use the direction provided by the TransferDescriptors. 13 Low speed 14 Skip 15 Isochronous 26:16 Maximum packet size 31:27 Reserved

The head pointer word contains:

Bits Field Meaning 0 Halted Processing of this endpoint's TransferDescriptor queue has halted. 1 Toggle carry Saved toggle for the next data packet: 0 means DATA0, 1 means DATA1. 3:2 Reserved Reserved. 31:4 TD address Address bits 31:4 of the next TransferDescriptor to process.

USB labels data packets DATA0 or DATA1 and alternates between them after each acknowledged packet. This lets the receiver recognize a retransmitted packet instead of accepting its data twice. See OHCI section 4.3.1.3.4, Sequence Bits.

Mask off the low four bits when extracting descriptor addresses. The low four bits of tail_pointer and next_endpoint are reserved.

You keep going until next_endpoint is null. Each EndpointDescriptor contains within it another linked list, defined by head_pointer and tail_pointer, of TransferDescriptors. Notably, tail_pointer is not the address of the last TransferDescriptor to process, it is a sentinel value. It is to be ignored once reached.

Logically, EndpointDescriptor can be thought of as a header that tells you what endpoint we are currently talking to, and how we're going to talk to it. TransferDescriptor then tells you "what" we're going to do it and what commands we want to do. A TransferDescriptor looks like this:

A general transfer descriptor occupies 16 bytes and is aligned to 16 bytes. Its words are little endian. Control, bulk and interrupt transfers use this layout; isochronous transfers use a different layout.

Byte offset Size Field Meaning 0x00 4 bytes flags Direction, completion status and transfer settings. 0x04 4 bytes current_buffer_pointer Physical address of the next data byte. Zero means no bytes remain. 0x08 4 bytes next_transfer Physical address of the next TransferDescriptor. Bits 3:0 are reserved. 0x0C 4 bytes buffer_end Physical address of the last byte in the buffer, inclusive.

The flags word contains:

Bits Field Meaning 17:0 Reserved Reserved. 18 Buffer rounding ??? 20:19 Direction 0: SETUP. 1: OUT. 2: IN. 3: reserved. Used when the ED defers to the TD. 23:21 Interrupt delay Completion interrupt delay in frames, 0–6. 7 requests no interrupt for this TD. 25:24 Data toggle 0 or 1: use the ED's toggle carry. 2: DATA0. 3: DATA1. 27:26 Error count Count of consecutive transaction errors. 31:28 Condition code Transfer completion status.

A condition code of zero indicates success to the IOS.

items.title: Transfer completion
items.text:
The controller walks the EndpointDescriptor list, processing each endpoint's TransferDescriptors one by one. If a device needs more time, the current descriptor stays pending and is retried later. Other endpoints can still make progress.

When a TransferDescriptor completes, the controller writes its condition code, advances the endpoint's head pointer, and adds it to the done list.

Its interrupt-delay field controls when to notify software: 0 means the next USB frame boundary, 1-6 adds that many milliseconds, and 7 requests no notification of its own. Multiple completions can share one notification. To notify software, the controller writes the done-list pointer into HCCA.done_head, a field in a shared structure in memory, and raises the Writeback Done Head interrupt.

items.title: Initial USB requests
items.text:
IOS initializes the Bluetooth module through control transfers on endpoint 0. The initial request types are:

Request Name Meaning 5 SET_ADDRESS Assign the device a USB address. IOS assigns 1; later EndpointDescriptors use that address to select it. 6 GET_DESCRIPTOR Read the device's identity and its available configuration, interfaces and endpoints. IOS can issue this request several times. 9 SET_CONFIGURATION Activate a configuration advertised by the device. IOS selects configuration 1.

Each request starts with an 8-byte request header in a SETUP TransferDescriptor. For GET_DESCRIPTOR, subsequent IN TransferDescriptors receive the requested bytes, followed by an empty OUT transfer acknowledging completion. SET_ADDRESS and SET_CONFIGURATION have no data stage and finish with an empty IN transfer. The new USB address takes effect after that final transfer completes, and thus concludes initialization.

items.title: SDI
items.text: SDI provides /dev/sdio/slot0 for the front SD slot at physical address 0x0D070000.

items.title: Interrupt dispatch
items.text:
dispatch_slot_interrupt (0x20400ED8) reads the low 16 bits of the word at 0x0D0700FC to find the slot that needs service:

Bits Field Firmware use 0 Slot 0 interrupt pending Services the current slot. 1 Slot 1 interrupt pending If bit 0 is clear, increments the slot index and services that slot.

If neither bit is set, the dispatcher stores -1 in the slot index and returns -1 without reading or acknowledging the normal interrupt status. An interrupt notification reaching IOS is not enough on its own. The slot status bit has to be set as well.

handle_slot_interrupt (0x20400AA0) saves the normal interrupt signal enable value and writes zero to the field. It reads the normal interrupt status and writes the sampled value back to acknowledge the pending events before it processes them. Before returning it restores the saved signal enable value.

Physical address Field SDI access 0x0D070030 Normal Interrupt Status Reads and acknowledges the low 16 bits. 0x0D070038 Normal Interrupt Signal Enable Saves, clears and restores the low 16 bits. 0x0D0700FC Slot Interrupt Status Reads the low 16 bits to select the slot.

read_register16 (0x20400CC0) reads the aligned 32 bit word and extracts the selected half. write_register16 (0x20400CDC) reads the containing word, replaces the selected half and writes the whole word back.

items.title: Command and transfer completion
items.text:
Normal interrupt bit Meaning Firmware action 0 Command complete Copies the four response words at offsets 0x10 through 0x1C into the pending request's response buffer. Completes the request unless a data transfer is still pending. 1 Transfer complete Clears the pending data state and marks the request complete. 3 DMA boundary Reads the DMA address at offset 0x00 and writes it back.

Offsets are relative to the selected slot's register base. Command completion and transfer completion are separate events, so a request with a pending data transfer is not complete until transfer complete arrives.

items.title: Block reads
items.text:
start_command (0x20400534) turns a CMD18 read with a block count of one into CMD17 before submitting it. Reads of more than one block keep CMD18.

For a data transfer it writes the DMA buffer address at offset 0x00, the block size at 0x04 and the block count at 0x06. It then writes the command argument at 0x08 and submits the combined transfer mode and command word at 0x0C. These offsets are relative to the selected slot's register base.

items.title: Block writes
items.text: start_command turns a CMD25 write with a block count of one into CMD24. Writes of more than one block keep CMD25. Writes use the same DMA, block-size and block-count registers as reads.

items.title: Write protection
items.text:
The routine reads Present State before submitting a data transfer:

Physical address Width Access Name 0x0D070024 32 bits R Present State Bit Field Firmware use 19 Write protect pin A clear bit rejects writes. A set bit allows them.

If bit 19 is clear, a write data transfer returns -10 before programming the DMA address or submitting the command. Reads are permitted regardless of this bit.

items.title: SO
items.text: SO provides the IOS socket service.

items.title: Thread records
items.text:
find_current_thread (0x13B5ADE8) obtains the current IOS thread ID through syscall 0x03. It searches g_network_threads (0x13B73D4C) from its first record and returns the address of the record with a matching thread ID. If no record matches, it calls the assertion handler. These virtual addresses refer to IOS80.

The table holds 27 big endian records with a stride of 20 bytes.

Offset Size Field Meaning 0x00 4 bytes Thread ID Index in the IOS kernel thread table 0x04 4 bytes Base priority Priority restored when releasing the network lock 0x08 4 bytes Last result Signed socket result for this thread 0x0C 4 bytes Next waiter Virtual pointer to the next thread record in a wait queue

register_network_thread (0x13B5AC14) stores the supplied thread ID and base priority in the first record whose signed thread ID is not positive. get_socket_result (0x13B4EEA4) looks up the current thread's record and returns its last result.

items.title: Network lock
items.text:
initialize_network_lock (0x13B5AD84) creates a message queue with a capacity of one message and sends the message 0 to it. g_network_lock_queue (0x13B73D44) holds the queue ID. The queued message acts as the lock token.

lock_network (0x13B5AD00) checks the current thread's priority. If it is already 56, the function returns 0 without receiving a message or changing the priority. Otherwise it receives the token with blocking enabled, raises the current thread's priority to 56 and returns 1.

unlock_network (0x13B5AC3C) returns 1 without changing any state if the current priority is not 56. Otherwise it finds the current thread's record, restores that record's base priority, sends the token back to the queue and returns 0. restore_network_lock (0x13B5AC88) calls unlock_network when its argument is nonzero and lock_network when its argument is zero.

For a thread whose base priority differs from 56, an uncontended lock and unlock pair executes the following syscalls.

Operation Syscall sequence Acquire Get priority (0x08), receive message (0x0E), set priority (0x09) Release Get priority (0x08), get thread ID (0x03), set priority (0x09), send message (0x0C)

items.title: Socket polling
items.text:
socket_worker (0x13B62238) dispatches IOCTL operation 0x0B to poll_sockets (0x13B51850). The output buffer holds an array of 12 byte big endian records. The record count is the buffer length divided by 12.

Offset Size Field 0x00 4 bytes Socket descriptor 0x04 4 bytes Requested events 0x08 4 bytes Returned events

The poll function accepts at most 24 records. It clears each returned-events field, retains valid socket objects and checks their readiness. It returns the number of records with a nonzero returned-events field. A zero timeout performs the readiness check without entering the wait queue, so the call returns 0 immediately if no socket is ready.

For one valid socket with a zero timeout, the normal path acquires and restores the network lock four times. It does so once to retain the socket, once to check readiness, once to release the protocol object's reference and once inside release_socket_node (0x13B4F20C). release_socket_node also looks up the current thread's record to store the node's last result there. When each lock restoration releases the lock, this path performs five thread record lookups in total.

items.title: SDIO initialization
items.text:
The WL wireless driver talks to the internal Wi-Fi chip through the SDIO host controller at 0x0D080000. In SDIO terms the chip is the card, so card selection, card interrupts and Card Inserted on this page all refer to it rather than the removable SD card.

init_sdio_card (0x13F1DD90) reads the 32 bit Present State register at 0x0D080024 and checks Card Inserted before continuing initialization.

Bits Field Meaning 16 Card Inserted 1 when the Wi-Fi chip is present. 0 stops initialization.

When Card Inserted is clear, the routine returns 1. attach_sdio_host (0x13F1E9D4) retries initialization once. If both attempts fail, it releases the host object and returns a null pointer. This failure propagates through the attachment routines.

wireless_worker (0x13F0A4E0) does not check the returned driver pointer before reading its message queue handle at offset 0x1C8. It calls receive_message (0x13F2869C) with that handle and retries immediately whenever the call returns a nonzero result.

items.title: Host setup
items.text:
Initialization checks the Capabilities register at 0x0D080040:

Bits Field Firmware use 5:0 Timeout Clock Frequency Must equal 48 for clock setup to proceed. 22 SDMA Support Must be set for initialization to proceed. 24 3.3 V Support Selects the 3.3 V power encoding when set. 25 3.0 V Support Selects the 3.0 V power encoding when bit 24 is clear. 26 1.8 V Support Selects the 1.8 V power encoding when bits 24 and 25 are clear.

reset_host (0x13F1D534) requests a card reset with CMD52, writing 8 to function 0 register 6. It then writes all three host reset bits and polls until they clear.

The word at 0x0D08002C contains the clock controls and reset requests used by WL:

Bits Field Firmware use 0 Internal Clock Enable Set before polling clock stability. 1 Internal Clock Stable Polled until set before enabling the card clock. 2 SD Clock Enable Set after the internal clock becomes stable. 19:16 Data Timeout Counter Value Written with 14 after card selection. 15:8 SDCLK Frequency Select Written with the clock divider encoding. 24 Software Reset For All Set during host reset. 25 Software Reset For CMD Line Set during host reset. 26 Software Reset For DAT Line Set during host reset.

After enabling the clock, WL selects a supported voltage and enables bus power through the word at 0x0D080028:

Bits Field Meaning 1 Data Transfer Width Set for a 4 bit bus. 8 SD Bus Power Set to enable power. 11:9 SD Bus Voltage Select 5 selects 1.8 V, 6 selects 3.0 V and 7 selects 3.3 V.

It then calls delay (0x13F0AA28) for 50,000 microseconds. This delay creates a timer and waits for a message on its completion queue before initialization continues.

items.title: Command completion and initialization failure
items.text:
After the power delay, initialization submits CMD5 with argument zero through send_command (0x13F1CF58). This writes 0x05020000 to 0x0D08000C and polls the lower halfword of the interrupt status register at 0x0D080030.

Bits Field Firmware use 1 Transfer Complete Wait for it after writing CMD53 data. 4 Buffer Write Ready Wait for it before writing CMD53 data to 0x0D080020. 5 Buffer Read Ready Wait for it before reading CMD53 data from 0x0D080020. 0 Command completion Wait for it to become set then acknowledge it by writing 1. 31:16 Error status Any nonzero value makes the completed command fail.

The polling counter starts at 5000 and is decremented after each read. If it reaches zero, the routine requests a command-line reset through the clock and reset register and returns 1. A command timeout makes card initialization fail. The attachment routine retries initialization once before returning a null pointer.

After completion, the routine checks error status. A nonzero error status causes it to return 1. With no error, probe_card (0x13F1DC8C) reads the CMD5 response. A zero response causes another CMD5 attempt. After 200 unsuccessful attempts, the probe returns 1 and initialization fails.

The worker's unchecked driver pointer then causes the receive loop to use a queue handle read from address 0x000001C8. If that handle is rejected, the worker immediately retries the receive call without blocking.

items.title: CMD5 response
items.text:
The CMD5 response is read from 0x0D080010. The probe and initialization routines use these fields:

Bits Field Firmware use 31 Ready Repeat CMD5 while clear. Return success when set. 30:28 I/O function count Require a nonzero count before continuing initialization. 21:20 Voltage window bits If either is set, submit CMD5 again with argument 0x00FFF000.

After the probe succeeds and the function count is nonzero, initialization proceeds to CMD3 with argument zero.

items.title: CMD3 response
items.text:
CMD3 publishes the card's relative address in its R6 response. WL submits it by writing 0x03020000 to 0x0D08000C with argument zero. After command completion, it reads the response from 0x0D080010 and checks these fields:

Bits Field Firmware use 31:16 Relative card address Save this value and use it in the upper halfword of the CMD7 argument. 15 Command CRC error Fail initialization when set. 14 Illegal command Fail initialization when set. 13 Error Fail initialization when set.

When the error fields are clear, initialization sends CMD7 to select the published address.

items.title: CMD7 response
items.text:
WL selects the card by writing 0x071A0000 to 0x0D08000C with the relative card address in the upper halfword of the argument. After completion, it requires the response at 0x0D080010 to equal 0x00001E00. Any other value makes initialization fail.

Bits Field Required value 12:9 Current state 15, indicating an I/O-only card

The comparison covers the entire response word, so every bit outside the current-state field must be clear.

items.title: CMD52 register access
items.text:
read_card (0x13F1D620) uses CMD52 for single byte reads and accesses to function 0. write_card (0x13F1D3AC) uses CMD52 for the corresponding writes. The host command word is 0x341A0000 after card selection. The argument at 0x0D080008 has these fields:

Bits Field Meaning 31 Write 1 writes a byte. 0 reads a byte. 30:28 Function Selects the I/O function. 27 Read after write Requests the register value after a write. WL clears this field in these helpers. 25:9 Register address Selects the byte within the function. 7:0 Data Byte to write.

The read helper takes the returned byte from bits 7:0 of the response at 0x0D080010.

After CMD7 succeeds, initialization performs these accesses through function 0:

  1. read_cis_pointer (0x13F1DD10) reads four bytes starting at 0x09 for the common Card Information Structure (CIS) pointer. It repeats this at function * 0x100 + 0x09 for each reported function. It interprets the bytes in little endian order and retains the low 17 bits.
  2. It writes 0x02 to I/O Enable at 0x02 to enable function 1.
  3. For a 4 bit bus, it reads Bus Interface Control at 0x07, replaces the width field with 2 and writes it back. It also sets Data Transfer Width in the host register.
  4. set_block_size (0x13F1CEEC) writes the low and high bytes of function 1's block size to 0x110 and 0x111. Initialization selects 64 bytes.
  5. With one reported function, it writes 0x03 to Interrupt Enable at 0x04.
Function 0 address Bits Field Value used during initialization 0x02 1 Function 1 enable 1 0x04 1 Function 1 interrupt enable 1 0x04 0 Master interrupt enable 1 0x07 1:0 Bus width 2 selects 4 bits.

items.title: CMD53 data reads
items.text:
For reads larger than one byte from a nonzero function, read_card submits CMD53 in byte mode with address increment enabled. The argument contains:

Bits Field Firmware use 31 Write Clear for reads. 30:28 Function Select the requested function. 27 Block mode Clear for byte mode. 26 Address increment Set. 25:9 Register address Select the first byte. 8:0 Count Requested byte count.

For a 4 byte read, the host block size is 4 and the block count is 1 in the low and high halfwords of 0x0D080004. The host command word is 0x353A0010.

After command completion, the polling path waits for Buffer Read Ready in the interrupt status register. It uses a counter initialized to 5000 and returns 1 if that counter expires. Once ready, it reads the word at 0x0D080020. It then reads normal interrupt status and acknowledges the set flags except Card Interrupt.

Bits Field Firmware use 8 Card Interrupt Excluded from the acknowledgement after a data read.

items.title: CMD53 data writes
items.text:
For writes larger than one byte to a nonzero function, write_card submits CMD53 with the same byte count and address fields as a read. It sets the Write field. For a 4 byte write, the host command word is 0x353A0000.

After command completion, the polling path waits for Buffer Write Ready. It uses a counter initialized to 5000 and returns 1 if that counter expires. It acknowledges Buffer Write Ready before writing the data at 0x0D080020. A 2 byte write uses the low halfword of that register. write_host_halfword (0x13F1CB18) does this as a 32 bit read-modify-write: it reads Buffer Data, replaces the low 16 bits and writes the whole word back. Buffer Data is therefore read in the middle of a write transfer.

The routine then polls Transfer Complete with another counter initialized to 5000. It leaves this loop when completion arrives or the counter expires. It acknowledges the set normal status flags except Card Interrupt and returns 0, including when this second counter expires.

items.title: Backplane access helpers
items.text:
read_backplane (0x13F1C8C4) and write_backplane (0x13F1C958) subtract 0x18000000 from the chip address and access SDIO function 1 through transfer_card (0x13F1D7AC). A successful read returns the low 8, 16 or 32 bits according to the requested size. A failed read returns 0xFFFFFFFF. The write helper returns 0 on success or -1 on failure.

For CMD53 accesses, the card helpers store the transfer size at byte offset 0x64 in the host object. The byte at 0x3A selects polling. With polling enabled, a successful read stores its result as a 32 bit word at the supplied output pointer. A 16 bit result occupies the low halfword of that word.

transfer_card reverses the four bytes of the data word for chip addresses 0x18001304, 0x1800130C, 0x18001314, 0x1800131C, 0x18001324, 0x1800132C, 0x18001334, 0x1800133C, 0x18001344, 0x1800134C, 0x18001354 and 0x1800135C. It changes the caller's data word in place before a write or after a read.

items.title: Card interrupt masking
items.text:
begin_card_access (0x13F1CE48) masks the card interrupt then increments the host object's access depth. end_card_access (0x13F1CE70) decrements the depth. If the result is zero and interrupts are enabled in the host object, it unmasks the card interrupt.

The host object uses native big endian fields:

Byte offset Size Field 0x0C 4 bytes Virtual address of the host register block 0x10 4 bytes Access depth 0x14 1 byte Nonzero requests interrupt unmasking when the access depth returns to zero 0x28 2 bytes Normal interrupt signal mask 0x3A 1 byte Nonzero selects polling for command and data completion 0x3D 1 byte Nonzero enables the mask/unmask register writes 0x64 4 bytes Transfer size in bytes

mask_card_interrupt (0x13F1CC0C) and unmask_card_interrupt (0x13F1CBE8) return without changing the mask when the byte at 0x3D is zero. Otherwise they update the Card Interrupt field in the stored mask then write it to the low halfword of Signal Enable at 0x0D080038, preserving the upper halfword.

Bits Field Firmware use 8 Card Interrupt Clear to mask and set to unmask the card interrupt signal.

items.title: PHY and radio identification
items.text:
attach_phy (0x13EFD5BC) reads the physical-layer hardware's version and radio identity before returning a PHY object. The following offsets are relative to the wireless core's base on the chip's internal backplane. WL accesses these registers through SDIO function 1.

Offset Width Firmware access Purpose 0x3E0 16 bits Read PHY version 0x3F6 16 bits Write Radio register selector 0x3F8 16 bits Read Upper half of the radio identity 0x3FA 16 bits Read Selected radio register data 0x3FC 16 bits Write PHY register selector 0x3FE 16 bits Read/write Selected PHY register data

The PHY version contains:

Bits Field Firmware use 15:12 Analog revision Save in the PHY object. 11:8 PHY type Accept 0, 1, 2 or 4 during attachment. 3:0 PHY revision Save for later compatibility checks.

For the 2.4 GHz attachment path, a rejected PHY type makes attach_phy release its allocation and return a null pointer. After PHY attachment, attach_wireless_core (0x13EDC774) accepts PHY revisions 1, 2, 6, 7 and 8.

When the chip package is neither 14 nor 15, attachment obtains the radio identity by writing selector 1 to 0x3F6 and reading 0x3F8. It writes selector 1 again before reading 0x3FA. The first read supplies the upper halfword and the second supplies the lower halfword:

uint32_t identity = ((uint32_t)upper << 16) | lower;
Bits Field Firmware use 31:28 Radio revision Save in the PHY object. 27:12 Radio number Require 0x2050 or 0x2055.

A rejected radio number makes attachment release its allocation and return a null pointer. Packages 14 and 15 instead select the internal identifier 0xE4F5 without this identity read.

items.title: Indirect PHY access
items.text:
read_phy (0x13EF54E0) writes a 16 bit register index to 0x3FC then reads 16 bits from 0x3FE. write_phy (0x13EF552C) writes the index followed by the value. Selecting an index and writing its data are separate operations.

set_phy_bits (0x13EF55DC) selects a register, reads its value and writes the bitwise OR of that value and its mask. mask_phy_bits (0x13EF557C) performs the corresponding bitwise AND. Both operate on 16 bit values.

items.title: Wireless core reset
items.text:
reset_core (0x13F24ADC) resets the selected core through its Target State Low register at backplane offset 0xF98:

Bits Field Firmware use 0 Reset Set during reset and cleared before the core is used. 16 Clock enable Kept set when releasing reset. 17 Force clocks Set during reset and cleared after reset is released.

After disabling the core, the routine writes the caller's core flags ORed with 0x00030001. It then clears any detected error conditions, writes the flags ORed with 0x00030000 and finally ORed with 0x00010000. After each of these three writes it reads Target State Low back and waits one microsecond.

During attachment, test_wireless_registers (0x13ED2D58) checks object data readback and the 16 bit views of the CFP start register. It then requires MAC control to read 0x00000400 or 0x80000400. Any other value fails the register test and with it the wireless core attachment.

items.title: MAC initialization
items.text:
WL accesses the wireless chip's MAC registers through SDIO function 1. These addresses belong to the chip's backplane.

Address Width Name Firmware use 0x18001120 32 bits MAC control Stop and start microcode execution. 0x18001128 32 bits Interrupt status Poll the microcode startup response. 0x18001160 32 bits Object address Select the destination for uploaded words. 0x18001164 32 bits Object data Write microcode and PCM data.

init_mac (0x13EDF148) writes 0x00000404 to MAC control before loading the microcode. load_microcode (0x13ED4CE0) writes object address 0x03000000 then streams the microcode through object data. load_pcm (0x13ED4D48) writes object address 0x000301EA and data 0x00004000 then selects 0x000301EB and streams the PCM data.

Every call to init_mac uploads both blocks. It does not check whether a previous call uploaded them. Each upload sends one 32 bit word per backplane write through write_card, producing a separate CMD53 transfer for each word. load_microcode uses the supplied byte count divided by four as its word count and returns the result of the final write. init_mac ignores the return values from both upload routines.

After uploading both blocks, initialization writes 0xFFFFFFFF to interrupt status and 0x00020402 to MAC control. It polls the following status field:

Bits Field Firmware use 0 MAC suspended End the startup wait when set.

The polling loop starts with a budget of 1000009. After each unsuccessful read, it subtracts 10 from the budget. If the previous budget exceeds 9, it delays for 10 microseconds before reading again. Otherwise it exits the loop. Initialization continues after either a set status bit or budget exhaustion.

items.title: HLE microcode upload shortcut
items.text:
WL spams microcode upload which really messes with performance so it's possible to HLE the microcode load mechanism (0x13ED4D1C) to counteract that!

int __fastcall load_microcode(int wireless, const unsigned int *data, unsigned int size)
{
  unsigned int word_count; // r5
  unsigned int index; // r4
  int result; // r0
  unsigned int word; // r3

  word_count = size >> 2;
  index = 0;
  for ( result = write_backplane(sdio: 0, address: *(_DWORD *)(wireless + 1956) + 352, size: 4u, value: 0x3000000u);
        index < word_count;
        result = write_backplane(sdio: 0, address: *(_DWORD *)(wireless + 1956) + 356, size: 4u, value: word) )
  {
    word = data[index++];
  }
  return result;
}

Basically you just do cpu.registers[4] = cpu.registers[5] - 1; lol.

items.title: MAC suspension
items.text:
suspend_mac (0x13ED0EDC) clears MAC control's enable field then polls the same MAC suspended status field. It delays for 10 microseconds between unsuccessful reads and stops after 3500 delays even if the status remains clear. It then reads MAC control and returns its value.

Register Bits Field Firmware use MAC control (0x18001120) 0 MAC enabled Clear before waiting for suspension.

items.title: MAC interrupts
items.text:
The wireless chip signals MAC events through the SDIO card interrupt. The host controller reports it in Card Interrupt (bit 8) of Normal Interrupt Status at 0x0D080030. It forwards it to Hollywood ARM interrupt 8 only while Card Interrupt is also set in Normal Interrupt Status Enable (0x0D080034) and Signal Enable (0x0D080038).

interrupt_worker (0x13F0A1B0) handles messages of type 2 by calling handle_host_interrupt (0x13F1EC14), which passes the host object to dispatch_card_interrupt (0x13F1E390). That routine returns early if Card Interrupt is clear in Normal Interrupt Status. Otherwise it saves Normal Interrupt Status Enable and clears its Card Interrupt bit. If the bytes at host object offsets 0x14 and 0x3D are both nonzero, it calls the card handler registered in the host object. It then restores the saved value, so Card Interrupt is disabled only while the handler runs.

Bits Field Firmware use 8 Card Interrupt Checked in 0x0D080030 and cleared in 0x0D080034 during handling.

The card handler card_interrupt (0x13F0A2A4) calls read_mac_interrupts (0x13ED7194), which does the following:

  1. It reads interrupt status at 0x18001128 and ANDs it with the driver's interrupt mask. If the read fails or the result is zero, it stops.
  2. It writes the masked value back to 0x18001128.
  3. If bit 15 is set in that value, it writes 0x00010000 to 0x18001020.
  4. It saves the masked value for process_mac_interrupts (0x13EF468C).
Bits Field Firmware use 15 Receive Read frames through the receive FIFO.

items.title: Channel selection
items.text:
The 16 bit register at 0x180013F0 holds the current channel, encoded as its center frequency minus 2400 MHz. Channel 1 is 0x000C, channel 6 is 0x0025 and channel 13 is 0x0048.

During an access point search, WL tunes to each channel as follows:

  1. Write 0x04020402 to MAC control, clearing MAC enabled.
  2. Write the channel value to 0x180013F0.
  3. Write 0x04020403 to MAC control, setting MAC enabled.

items.title: PIO receive FIFO
items.text:
WL receives frames through a programmed I/O receive FIFO in the wireless core.

Address Width Name Firmware use 0x18001308 32 bits Receive FIFO control Detect, accept and discard frames. 0x1800130C 32 bits Receive FIFO data Read the receive record of a frame. Bits Field Firmware use 0 Frame ready Read as 1 when a frame is waiting. Written as 1 to accept it. 1 Data ready Polled until set after accepting a frame. Written as 1 to discard a frame.

pio_receive (0x13F0D284) reads one frame as follows:

  1. It reads receive FIFO control and returns without a frame if Frame ready is clear.
  2. It writes 1 to receive FIFO control.
  3. It polls receive FIFO control for Data ready, reading up to 11 times with a 10 microsecond delay between reads. If Data ready never sets, it returns without a frame and without discarding it.
  4. It reads the first data word, takes the frame size from it and allocates a packet buffer with a packet length of the frame size plus 30.
  5. It stores the first word at buffer offset 0x00 and reads four more words into offsets 0x04 to 0x13.
  6. If bit 0 of the MAC status at offset 0x0C is set, it discards the frame.
  7. It reads the frame data into the buffer at offset 0x1E. If that address is not word aligned and the frame is longer than one byte, it first reads 2 bytes into 0x1E and continues at 0x20.
  8. It reads the remaining whole words, then one more word for any leftover bytes.

To discard a frame, the routine writes 2 to receive FIFO control and releases the packet buffer. It also discards the frame if allocation or a bulk read fails.

Depending on some random bullshit, the header and frame data are read either one 32 bit word at a time or with read_backplane_bulk (0x13F1C9B8). Every read targets 0x1800130C. Each path stores the record bytes in the order the card sends them:

  • A single read passes through the byte reversal in transfer_card and is stored as a native big endian word.
  • read_backplane_bulk calls transfer_extended (0x13F1E434) for a CMD53 read of function 1 at a fixed address. It uses byte mode for transfers shorter than function 1's block size or for all transfers when the host object disables block mode. The routine waits for Buffer Read Ready, acknowledges it, reads the words from Buffer Data at 0x0D080020 and reverses the bytes of each word itself.
  • A bulk transfer of at least one block uses block mode, with SDMA when the host object enables DMA. For SDMA, send_command writes the bounce buffer's address to 0x0D080000 and sets transfer mode bit 0. After Transfer Complete, transfer_extended acknowledges Transfer Complete and DMA Interrupt by writing 0x000A to 0x0D080030 and copies the bounce buffer to the destination without byte reversal.

The transfer mode bits occupy the low halfword of the command word at 0x0D08000C:

Bits Field Firmware use 0 DMA Enable Set for block mode CMD53 transfers when DMA is enabled. 1 Block Count Enable Set when the block count exceeds one. 4 Data Transfer Direction Set for reads. 5 Multiple Block Set when the block count exceeds one.

A single block SDMA read therefore uses transfer mode 0x0011. In block mode, 0x0D080004 holds the block size in its low halfword and the block count from the CMD53 argument in its upper halfword.

items.title: Receive record
items.text:
The receive record is a 20 byte header followed by the frame data. Header fields are 16 bit little endian values.

Offset Size Firmware use 0x00 2 bytes Frame size, the number of frame data bytes after the header. 0x04 2 bytes PHY status 0, used for the signal strength. 0x06 2 bytes PHY status 1, used for the signal strength. 0x0A 2 bytes PHY status 3, used for the signal strength. 0x0C 2 bytes MAC status. MAC status bits Firmware use 0 Discard the frame. 2 Two padding bytes precede the frame data.

The frame data starts with a 6 byte physical layer header, followed by the 802.11 frame and its frame check sequence. Before parsing, WL converts the header halfwords from little endian to native order. It then skips the 30 bytes that precede the frame data, plus 2 more if the padding bit is set.

items.title: Scan results
items.text:
WL finds and joins networks through 802.11 management frames such as beacons and probe responses. It passes them to receive_management (0x13EF30F4). A probe response is added to the scan results by add_scan_result (0x13ED9170) when both of these conditions hold:

  • The word at driver object offset 0x143C is not -1.
  • The frame's first address equals the station address at driver object offset 0x24.

A beacon is added only when bit 2 of the byte at driver object offset 0x1442 is also set. parse_bss_info (0x13ED8A18) reads the advertised network's capability information, SSID, supported rates and DS parameter set.

items.title: Joining an open network
items.text:
For an open-system connection, WL authenticates before sending an association request. set_association_state (0x13ED1160) stores the current state at driver object offset 0xF7C. The successful station path uses these states and events:

State Expected response Successful event Next state 2 Open-system authentication response with transaction sequence 2. 3 5 5 Association response. 7 6 6 Beacon from the selected BSSID. 1 followed by 0 0

receive_management checks the selected BSSID before accepting these responses. A successful association response stores its association ID at driver object offset 0x1A56. process_wireless_event (0x13EE02D4) handles the success event through activate_association (0x13EE1418), which enters state 6 for the station connection.

Association alone does not complete the join. In state 6, a beacon from the selected BSSID reaches complete_join_from_beacon (0x13EE39EC). It emits event 1 with status zero. For an initial join, the event handler emits event 0 with status zero and returns the association state to 0.

items.title: Signal strength
items.text:
compute_rssi (0x13F02660) derives a signed signal strength from the converted receive header. For radio 0x2050, when bit 0 of PHY status 0 is set:

int rssi = (int8_t)(phy_status_1 & 0xFF);
if (phy_status_3 & 0x0400)
    rssi += 17;
else
    rssi -= 4;
Field Bits Firmware use PHY status 0 0 Select the direct signed sample when set. PHY status 1 7:0 Signed sample before the radio correction. PHY status 3 10 Add 17 when set. Subtract 4 when clear.

items.title: HLE frame reception
items.text:
A microcode HLE can deliver management and data frames through this receive path. The other interfaces it has to provide are covered under Microcode HLE.

To deliver a frame:

  1. Queue a receive record made of a 20 byte header, a 6 byte physical layer header, the 802.11 frame and a 4 byte frame check sequence. WL accepts a physical layer header and frame check sequence filled with zeros. The frame size covers everything after the 20 byte header.
  2. Set Frame ready in receive FIFO control and set bit 15 of interrupt status at 0x18001128.
  3. If the MAC interrupt mask enables bit 15, raise the SDIO card interrupt, subject to the host controller enables described under MAC interrupts.
  4. After WL writes 1 to receive FIFO control, report Data ready.
  5. Serve every read of 0x1800130C from the next bytes of the record, whether it is a single word, a 16 byte read in byte mode or an SDMA read in block mode. Drop the record once its last byte has been read or when WL writes 2.

To make an access point appear in the search, send a probe response addressed to the station address while WL is tuned to the access point's channel and MAC enabled is set again. To report a signal strength on radio 0x2050, set PHY status 0 bit 0, clear PHY status 3 bit 10 and store the desired value plus 4 as a signed 8 bit value in PHY status 1 bits 7:0.

items.title: Frame transmission
items.text:
WL uses six PIO FIFOs. For FIFO index n from 0 through 5, the transmit registers have these wireless backplane addresses:

Address Width Access Purpose 0x18001300 + 0x10 * n 32 bits R/W Transmit control. 0x18001304 + 0x10 * n 32 bits W Transmit data.

pio_transmit (0x13F0CD8C) submits a packet chain through the selected FIFO. It writes 0x00000080 to transmit control before copying data and writes 0x00000010 after the final fragment. Between these writes it selects the valid bytes of each data word through the low four control bits:

Bits Firmware use 3:0 Byte enables. Bit n selects byte n of the data word. 4 Submit the accumulated frame. 7 Start writing a frame.

For an unaligned fragment, WL enables only the occupied lanes of its first aligned word. It then enables all four lanes while transferring complete words and enables only the occupied lanes of the final word. Fragment boundaries do not submit the frame. transfer_card (0x13F1D7AC) reverses the byte order of individual PIO data writes so the FIFO receives packet bytes in memory order. Bulk transfers through transfer_fifo (0x13F1CA18) use fixed-address CMD53 writes to the same data register.

build_transmit_header (0x13ED5D04) prepends a 100 byte transmit header and a 6 byte physical layer header to the 802.11 frame. Offsets are relative to the start of the transmit record. The frame ID and status are little endian:

Byte offset Size Field 0x48 2 bytes Frame ID. 0x4A 2 bytes Initial transmit status, set to zero. 0x64 6 bytes Physical layer header. 0x6A Variable 802.11 frame.

The frame ID's low three bits select the FIFO. After submission, WL retains the packet in that FIFO's software queue until transmit completion. process_transmit_status (0x13EE17AC) selects the queue from the returned frame ID and releases a completed packet. release_pio_transmit (0x13F0CA7C) decrements the queued frame count and subtracts the packet chain length rounded up to a multiple of four from the queued byte count.

Frame ID bits Meaning 2:0 Transmit FIFO index.

items.title: FIFO capacity
items.text:
During init_mac, write_initial_registers (0x13ED2268) programs shared memory through the object registers. One sequence writes object address 0x03010025 then writes 0x00320000, 0x090A0E09 and 0x0000060E to object data. The streamed words occupy consecutive shared memory word pairs starting at byte offset 0x94.

read_shm_bytes (0x13ED4DF4) reads six bytes starting at shared memory byte offset 0x98. init_mac multiplies each byte by 256 to initialize a FIFO's capacity when its software capacity is zero:

FIFO Shared memory byte offset Capacity byte Capacity 0 0x98 0x09 2304 bytes 1 0x99 0x0E 3584 bytes 2 0x9A 0x0A 2560 bytes 3 0x9B 0x09 2304 bytes 4 0x9C 0x0E 3584 bytes 5 0x9D 0x06 1536 bytes

pio_has_space (0x13F0C9CC) rejects a submission that would exceed 32 queued frames or the FIFO's byte capacity. For one frame it rounds the packet chain length up to a multiple of four bytes. It also rejects submission while transmit control bit 8 is set.

Transmit control bits Firmware use 8 Suspend transmission. A set bit prevents further submissions.

items.title: Delays
items.text:
delay uses a timer and a message queue for requests above 1,000 microseconds. It creates a queue with one message slot, starts a one-shot timer and blocks waiting for its message. It destroys the timer and queue before returning.

For requests of at most 1,000 microseconds, it polls timer syscall 0x15. It converts the requested duration to ticks as follows:

uint32_t ticks = microseconds * 19 / 10;
if (ticks <= 20)
    ticks -= ticks / 4;

It reads a starting counter value. If ticks is zero, it returns without polling. Otherwise each poll computes current - start with 32 bit unsigned wraparound. If the signed 32 bit value of current is less than or equal to the signed value of start, it subtracts one more tick from that difference. Polling ends when the adjusted unsigned difference is at least ticks. Equal counter samples therefore produce 0xFFFFFFFF and end the wait.

Firmware delay IOS80 v6944 0x13F0AA28 IOS70 v6687 0x13F0A9F4

items.title: Microcode HLE
items.text: During MAC initialization, WL uploads a microcode image to the wireless core. The microcode runs on the core's programmable state machine and handles medium access and transmission, acknowledgements, receive filtering and building the receive header that precedes every frame in the receive FIFO. WL never calls into the microcode directly. It talks to it through shared memory, MAC control, the MAC command register, interrupt status and the FIFOs. A high-level emulation (HLE) of the microcode has to provide these interfaces.

items.title: Image
items.text:
g_microcode (0x13F29DF0) holds 0x5D00 bytes, which is 2976 instructions of 8 bytes each. WL uploads it to offset 0 of microcode memory. On this page, microcode addresses are byte offsets into microcode memory and WL addresses are Starlet virtual addresses in IOS80. Execution starts at reset (0x0000), which clears the GPIO output and jumps to init (0x4078).

During startup, the microcode publishes its version in shared memory:

Word Name Value 0x000 UCODEREV 0x014B 0x001 UCODEPATCH 0x0196 0x002 UCODEDATE 0x7915 0x003 UCODETIME 0x915D

items.title: Shared memory
items.text:
Shared memory is an array of 16 bit words. The microcode addresses it by word index, while the host uses byte offsets, so word n sits at byte offset 2n. The host selects a word through the object address register and then accesses one halfword of the object data register. write_shm (0x13ED01C4) and read_shm (0x13ED03F4) take an even byte offset and work like this, with the driver argument omitted:

void write_shm(uint32_t offset, uint16_t value)
{
    write32(0x18001160, 0x00010000 | (offset >> 2));
    write16((offset & 2) ? 0x18001166 : 0x18001164, value);
}

uint16_t read_shm(uint32_t offset)
{
    write32(0x18001160, 0x00010000 | (offset >> 2));
    return read16((offset & 2) ? 0x18001166 : 0x18001164);
}

The byte representation of each shared memory word is little endian. For example, shm[0x0C0] = 0x0039 stores the 16 bit value 0x0039 at byte offset 0x180, represented by bytes 39 00.

These words make up the host interface:

Word Byte offset Name Microcode use WL use 0x000-0x003 0x00-0x06 Version words Written by init. init_mac (0x13EDF148) reads UCODEREV and UCODEPATCH. 0x01A 0x34 Receive pad offset Added to the receive length of padded frames. 0x020 0x40 UCODESTAT Current microcode state. Polled after waking the MAC. 0x028 0x50 PHYVER Bits 7:0 of the PHY version, written by init. 0x029 0x52 PHYTYPE Bits 11:8 of the PHY version, written by init. 0x044-0x046 0x88-0x8C JSSI 0, 1 and AUX Results of the noise measurement.

init_mac (0x13EDF148) reads the version words after its startup wait and combines them into one word, with UCODEREV in the high halfword and UCODEPATCH in the low halfword. The wait also ends on timeout, so these reads can happen before startup has actually finished.

items.title: UCODESTAT
items.text:
Value State Written by 1 Init init, after clearing shared memory. 3 Suspended suspend (0x3778), after raising interrupt status bit 0. 2 Active suspend once MAC enabled is set. Also the power save routine (0x42E0) when it wakes. 4 Sleep The power save routine, before its sleep loop.

update_power_save (0x13ED045C) updates MAC control bits 25 and 26. If it sets bit 26 while bit 25 was already set and bit 26 was clear, it waits 40 microseconds and then polls UCODESTAT until it reads a value other than 4. It reads at most 27 times with a 10 microsecond delay between reads and gives up after the last read without delaying again. Both waits go through the WL delay helper.

items.title: MAC control
items.text:
WL accesses MAC control at backplane address 0x18001120. The microcode reads its upper half through register 0x041.

MAC control bits Microcode use 0 MAC enabled. The suspended loop waits for this bit to be set. 23 Keep frames with a bad frame check sequence. 25 Enable the power save path. 26 Request that the MAC stay awake. WL polls UCODESTAT when waking it. 29 Skip writing transmit status entries in finish_tx (0x1F58). 31 Select the G-mode register bank used by noise measurement.

items.title: Host flags
items.text: Shared memory word Bits Use 0x02F 15 Defer the current transmit status entry. 0x030 9 Enable the radio switch check in the main loop.

items.title: Interrupts raised by the microcode
items.text:
The microcode raises interrupt status bits at 0x18001128 by writing microcode register 0x042 for bits 15:0 and 0x043 for bits 31:16. The routines on this page raise these bits:

Bit Raised by Condition 0 suspend (0x3778) Every entry into the suspended state. 7 finish_tx (0x1F58) Reaching the status reporting path at 0x1FB0. 8 transfer_rx_header (0x41E0) A header transfer completed without overflow.

The measurement commands raise their own completion interrupts only once a requested measurement finishes.

The microcode never raises bit 15 or bit 29 itself, even though WL relies on both. Bit 15 tells WL to drain the receive FIFO and bit 29 tells it to read transmit status. They are separate from bits 8 and 7, which the microcode raises on receive and transmit respectively.

items.title: Startup and suspension
items.text:
init runs after reset. The pseudocode below covers its shared memory setup and leaves out internal engine setup. Here and in later examples, helpers and header fields without a firmware address are pseudocode names. read_external() is the microcode's indirect read of a core register, where index 0 is the PHY version.

// 0x4078
void init(void)
{
    for (int word = 0x7FF; word >= 0; word--)
        shm[word] = 0;

    shm[UCODESTAT] = 1;

    uint16_t phy_version = read_external(0);
    shm[PHYVER] = phy_version & 0xFF;
    shm[PHYTYPE] = (phy_version >> 8) & 0xF;

    shm[0x0C0] = 0x0039;
    shm[0x0C2] = 0x0050;
    shm[0x0C4] = 0xFC00;
