    shm[0x011] = 0xFF00;
    if (shm[PHYTYPE] == 2 && (microcode_register[0x01C] & 0x0100) && shm[PHYVER] == 0)
        shm[0x011] = 0;

    shm[UCODEREV] = 0x014B;
    shm[UCODEPATCH] = 0x0196;
    shm[UCODEDATE] = 0x7915;
    shm[UCODETIME] = 0x915D;

    goto suspend;
}
Source Bits Initialization use PHY version 7:0 Stored in PHYVER. PHY version 11:8 Stored in PHYTYPE. Microcode register 0x01C 8 With PHYTYPE 2 and PHYVER 0, selects zero for shared memory word 0x011.

Clearing shared memory wipes anything the host wrote to words 0x000 through 0x7FF before startup. WL writes its shared memory configuration after the startup wait in init_mac.

suspend (0x3778) reports the suspended state and waits for the host. resume (0x37B8) follows directly:

// 0x3778
suspend:
    raise_interrupt(0);
    shm[UCODESTAT] = 3;
    while (!mac_enabled())
        ;
    shm[UCODESTAT] = 2;

// 0x37B8
resume:
    reset_rx();
    goto main_events;

mac_enabled() tests MAC control bit 0. The first pass through suspend raises interrupt status bit 0, which init_mac polls for after starting the microcode.

reset_rx (0x37F0) clears the microcode's internal branch state and condition latches, resets receive processing and empties the queue of pending probe responses.

When the main loop sees MAC enabled clear, it branches to mac_disabled (0x3760), which leads into suspend. suspend_mac (0x13ED0EDC) waits for the resulting interrupt before it proceeds. Setting MAC enabled again writes UCODESTAT 2 and resumes execution.

items.title: Main loop
items.text:
main_loop (0x0010) checks hardware and software work flags before sleeping. main_events (0x0048) checks for the following work in order. A taken branch can skip the remaining checks.

  1. The radio hardware switch, when the host flag enables its check.
  2. Deferred transmit status and acknowledgements.
  3. MAC enabled. When it is clear, the loop enters mac_disabled.
  4. A transmit FIFO flush request.
  5. Transmit events at tx_events (0x0140).
  6. Receive events at rx_events (0x0180), including begin_rx (0x27A0) and finish_rx (0x2D88).
  7. The MAC commands for noise measurement and clear channel assessment.
  8. Beacon interval events and the start of the next transmission.

items.title: Receive
items.text:
begin_rx (0x27A0) runs at the start of a frame. It latches the 64 bit timing synchronization function (TSF) timer, builds the receive header's channel word and waits until 0x26 bytes have arrived or the frame is complete. It then clears both MAC status words. If at least 0x10 bytes arrived, it reads the frame control field and classifies the frame.

finish_rx (0x2D88) runs at the end of the frame. It records the receive timestamp, checks the frame check sequence, applies address filtering and fills in the remaining header fields. A frame that fails address filtering is dropped before it reaches the FIFO. A frame with a bad frame check sequence is only kept when MAC control bit 23 is set. It is then marked with MAC status bit 0, which makes pio_receive (0x13F0D284) discard it.

The normal header path starts at 0x3090. This excerpt shows the length and PHY status writes. Internal receive state can still divert execution before the header transfer.

// finish_rx, normal header construction
shm[RXHDR_LENGTH] = rx_byte_count;
if (padding_inserted) {
    shm[RXHDR_LENGTH] += shm[0x01A];
    shm[RXHDR_MAC_STATUS_LOW] |= 0x0004;
}
shm[RXHDR_PHY_STATUS_0] = phy_status[0];
shm[RXHDR_PHY_STATUS_1] = phy_status[1];
shm[RXHDR_PHY_STATUS_2] = phy_status[2];
shm[RXHDR_PHY_STATUS_3] = phy_status[3];
transfer_rx_header();

transfer_rx_header (0x41E0) hands the prepared receive header to the receive engine without the frame body. It returns immediately if bit 9 of internal register r45 is set. Otherwise it points the engine at the 10 word header in shared memory, starts the transfer and waits for the busy condition to set and then clear. It checks for receive overflow throughout this wait and once more before raising interrupt status bit 8.

void transfer_rx_header(void)
{
    if (skip_rx_header)
        return;

    rx_header_source = 0x548;
    rx_header_words = 10;
    rx_header_control = 1;

    do {
        if (receive_overflow_pending())
            goto overflow;
    } while (!header_transfer_busy());
    do {
        if (receive_overflow_pending())
            goto overflow;
    } while (header_transfer_busy());
    if (receive_overflow_pending())
        goto overflow;
    raise_interrupt(8);
    return;

overflow:
    handle_receive_overflow();
}

The pseudocode names map to these internal fields:

Register Bits Pseudocode field Use r45 9 skip_rx_header Return without transferring a header or raising bit 8. 0x007 15:0 rx_header_source Shared memory word index 0x548. 0x008 15:0 rx_header_words Header length of 10 words. 0x004 1:0 rx_header_control Set to 1 to begin the header transfer.

header_transfer_busy() tests microcode condition 0x0B and receive_overflow_pending() tests condition 0x0D. handle_receive_overflow() is a branch to rx_overflow (0x3728), which leaves the helper without raising the interrupt or returning normally.

items.title: Receive header
items.text:
The header occupies shared memory words 0x548 to 0x551 and forms the first 20 bytes of the receive record:

Word Record offset Field Source 0x548 0x00 Frame size Received byte count, plus the receive pad offset for padded frames. 0x54A 0x04 PHY status 0 PHY receive status register 0 (microcode register 0x009). 0x54B 0x06 PHY status 1 PHY receive status register 1 (microcode register 0x00A). 0x54C 0x08 PHY status 2 PHY receive status register 2 (microcode register 0x01A). 0x54D 0x0A PHY status 3 PHY receive status register 3 (microcode register 0x01B). 0x54E 0x0C MAC status See below. 0x550 0x10 Receive time Low 16 bits of the TSF timer latched at reception (microcode register 0x11F). 0x551 0x12 Channel word See below. MAC status bits Meaning 0 The frame check sequence did not match. 1 The microcode started a response to this frame. 2 Padding was inserted before the frame data. Channel word bits Source 1:0 Bits 1:0 of PHYTYPE. 9:2 Bits 7:0 of external register 0x08. 14:10 Bits 4:0 of external register 0x25.

items.title: Transmit completion
items.text:
finish_tx (0x1F58) handles the frame at the head of the current transmit FIFO. On the status reporting path, it sets status bit 6 if the frame has to stay at the head and otherwise asks for it to be released. It then raises interrupt status bit 7. MAC control bit 29 skips the status entry writes but not the interrupt.

count_tx_attempt (0x4248) increments one of the status word's two 4 bit attempt counters, selected by the transmit state. Each counter wraps within its 4 bits. Probe responses take a separate path that increments shared memory word 0x560 instead.

At 0x1FF8, finish_tx copies bit 0 of the internal status into bit 1 of the status entry. Before handling the current entry, it calls report_saved_tx_status (0x4B10) to write out any previously saved one. If host flag 0x02F bit 15 is set, the current entry is saved in shared memory for that helper to report later. Otherwise it is written immediately:

uint16_t status = header.status;
status = (status & ~0x0002) | ((status & 0x0001) << 1);
report_saved_tx_status();
if (defer_tx_status) {
    save_tx_status(status & ~0x0001, header);
} else {
    tx_status[3] = header.word_28;
    tx_status[2] = header.word_27;
    tx_status[1] = header.word_24;
    tx_status[0] = status | 0x0001;
}

save_tx_status() stands for the shared memory writes and setting the pending flag. The header.word_* suffixes are word offsets into the microcode's copy of the current transmit header, where the status word sits at offset 0x25. An entry goes to these registers when written immediately and to these shared memory words when saved:

Microcode register Value Saved shared memory word 0x08F Header word 0x28 0x564 0x08E Header word 0x27 0x563 0x08D Header word 0x24 0x562 0x08C Status with valid bit set 0x561 with bit 0 set

report_saved_tx_status does nothing if r45 bit 0 is clear. Otherwise it writes the saved words to the registers in the order above and clears the pending flag.

Register Bits Meaning r45 0 A saved transmit status entry is pending. Status bits Meaning 15:12 Attempt counter. 11:8 Attempt counter. 6 The frame stays at the head of its FIFO. 1 Copy of bit 0 of the internal status. 0 Valid. Set when the entry is reported.

On interrupt status bit 29, WL's process_mac_interrupts (0x13EF468C) reads transmit status entries. For each one, it reads 0x18001170 and stops if bit 0 is clear. Otherwise it reads the entry from 0x18001174 and processes it. With a nonzero work limit argument, it reads at most eight entries per call.

Register Bits WL use 0x18001170 0 Continue reading a status entry when set. Stop when clear.

The two reads provide these fields to WL's process_transmit_status (0x13EE17AC):

Register Bits Field 0x18001170 31:16 Frame ID from the transmit header. 0x18001170 15:0 Transmit status. 0x18001174 15:0 Sequence value. Transmit status bits WL use 15:12 Frame transmit attempt count. 6 Intermediate report. WL retains the queued packet. 1 Acknowledged transmission. 0 Valid entry.

items.title: MAC commands
items.text:
The main loop reads host commands from the MAC command register (microcode register 0x047). Each measurement routine below returns immediately unless its command bit is set. When the measurement completes, it writes the bit back to clear it and raises the matching interrupt.

Command bit Routine Completion 3 measure_cca (0x54F8) Clears bit 3 and raises interrupt status bit 17. 4 measure_noise (0x5328) Clears bit 4 and raises interrupt status bit 18.

measure_noise (0x5328) measures background noise. The pseudocode shows the path for PHY types other than 0. All shared memory words and TSF timer halves are unsigned 16 bit values. wait_for_noise_sample(us, ignore_ifs) waits until the low half of the TSF timer reaches its starting value plus us, modulo 65536. It returns false early if condition 0x20 is set or if interframe space status bit 11 is set while ignore_ifs is false.

void measure_noise(void)
{
    if (!(mac_command & 0x0010))
        return;
    if (!noise_pending) {
        noise_pending = true;
        read_tsf_low();
        shm[0x569] = read_tsf_high();
    }
    read_tsf_low();
    uint16_t elapsed_high = read_tsf_high() - shm[0x569];

    shm[JSSI_AUX] = (read_external(0x08) & 0xFF)
        | ((read_external(gmode ? 0x45F : 0x05F) & 0xFF) << 8);

    int word = 0x044;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
        if (!wait_for_noise_sample(2, elapsed_high >= 2))
            return;
        shm[word] = (shm[word] & ~0x01FF) | (read_external(0x27) & 0x01FF);
        shm[word] = rotate_right_16(shm[word], 8);
        word ^= 1;
    }
    if (elapsed_high < 2 && !wait_for_noise_sample(24, false))
        return;

    mac_command = 0x0010;
    raise_interrupt(18);
    noise_pending = false;
}

The four samples alternate between JSSI 0 and JSSI 1. gmode is MAC control bit 31 as latched when the microcode left suspend. The final 24 microsecond wait is skipped when elapsed_high, computed once on entry, is at least 2. An interrupted pass leaves the command bit and pending flag set, so the next call takes a fresh set of samples while keeping the original timestamp.

Register Bits Pseudocode field or use r20 3 noise_pending, retaining the initial timestamp across interrupted passes. 0x148 11 Interframe space condition that aborts a wait unless ignored as described above.

measure_cca (0x54F8) performs clear channel assessment. On completion it writes 0x4000 to microcode register 0x133, updates registers 0x136 and 0x137, clears command bit 3 and raises interrupt status bit 17. It does not modify the JSSI words.

items.title: HLE
items.text:
An HLE has to provide the following behavior to WL and keep the microcode's own interrupts separate from the FIFO notifications:

Routine Address Behavior exposed to WL init 0x4078 Clear shared memory, publish the version words and PHY identity, then enter suspend. suspend, resume 0x3778, 0x37B8 Raise interrupt bit 0 and write UCODESTAT 3 when suspending. Write UCODESTAT 2 on resume. transfer_rx_header 0x41E0 Supply the receive header and raise bit 8 only once its transfer completes. WL drains receive records on bit 15. finish_tx 0x1F58 Report transmit status and raise bit 7. WL reads the status on interrupt bit 29.

HLE frame reception describes how to deliver scan results through the receive FIFO.

items.title: CDROM Commands
items.text:
The following commands seem to be required as a bare minimum:

cmd     subcmd  irq     result fifo
----------------------------------------------
0x01            INT3    Status
0x19    0x20    INT3    Get cdrom BIOS date/version (yy,mm,dd,ver)

items.title: Further Notes & Code
items.text:
• I return [0x69, 0x69, 0x69, 0x69] for the CDROM version
  • I set only the "Shell Open" bit for status
  • I send both "acknowledge" and "complete" IRQs (with an arbitrary 1000 cycle delay inbetween)
  • I update parameter readiness bits on every tick
fn execute_command(&mut self, command: u8) {
    match command {
        // 0x01     Nop         INT3: status
        0x01 => {
            self.pending_command = Some(command);
            self.send_status(&[]);
            self.trigger_irq(DiskIrq::CommandAcknowledged);
        }
        // 0x19     Test *  sub, ...    INT3: ...
        0x19 => {
            let subcommand = self.parameter_fifo.pop_front().unwrap();
            self.execute_subcommand(subcommand);
        }
        _ => {
            tracing::error!(
                target: "psx_core::cdrom",
                command = format!("{:02X}", command),
                "Unimplemented CDROM command",
            );
        }
    }

    self.address.set_busy_status(true);
}

fn execute_subcommand(&mut self, subcommand: u8) {
    match subcommand {
        0x20 => {
            self.result_fifo.push_back(0x69); // year
            self.result_fifo.push_back(0x69); // month
            self.result_fifo.push_back(0x69); // day
            self.result_fifo.push_back(0x69); // version
            self.trigger_irq(DiskIrq::CommandAcknowledged);
        }
    }
}

pub fn tick(&mut self, cycles: usize) {
    self.address.set_parameter_empty(self.parameter_fifo.is_empty());
    self.address.set_parameter_write_ready(self.parameter_fifo.len() < 16);
    self.cycles += cycles;

    if self.cycles >= CYCLE_DELAY {
        self.cycles -= CYCLE_DELAY;

        if let Some(command) = self.pending_command.take() {
            self.parameter_fifo.clear();
            self.address.set_busy_status(false);
            self.address.set_data_request(true);
            self.address.set_result_read_ready(true);

            self.trigger_irq(DiskIrq::CommandCompleted);
        }
    }
}

items.title: BIOS Stuck in Loop
items.text:
Stubbed GPUSTAT (0xFFFF_FFFF) will eventually lead to this:

loc_8004FE44:
lw      $a4, 0($a1)
addiu   $v1, $v1, 1
xor     $a5, $v0, $a4
and     $a6, $a5, $a0
beq     $a6, $zero, loc_8004FE44
nop

where:

  • a0 is 0x8000_0000
  • a1 points to GPUSTAT register
  • v0 is original GPUSTAT value

Basically waits for bit 31 to change.

In 480-lines mode, bit31 changes per frame. And in 240-lines mode, the bit changes per scanline. The bit is always zero during Vblank (vertical retrace and upper/lower screen border).

Seems to be 240-lines mode in my case. We get here because of the start of that routine:

sub_8004FE08:
lw      $v0, 0($a1)
bne     $a0, $zero, loc_8004FF00
lui     $at, 8
and     $t6, $v0, $at
beq     $t6, $zero, loc_8004FE64
nop

Roughly translates to (same register meaning as above): 

if ( (*GPUSTAT & 0x80000) != 0 ) {
  // Deadlock here...
}

It checks bit 19, if it's not 0 it will start waiting for something. This bit indicates vertical resolution:

  • 0 = 240 lines (what it should be according to my emulator atm)
  • 1 = 480 lines

So if the vertical resolution is 480 lines it will start waiting for a new frame presumably? Since the next bit change (bit 31) would be during VBLANK (???). Since GPUSTAT is stubbed it will always think we are in 480 lines mode. 0x1480_2000 seems to work better as an early stub (reset value?) but breaks the amidog CPU tests unless bit 27 which indicates VRAM to CPU DMA readiness is forcefully set as well.

Note: BIOS does swap to 480-lines mode eventually, so can't really escape it for long.

items.title: Calculating Polygon Word Count
items.text:
Polygon primitive base count is calculated based on vertices count bit:

pub struct DrawPolygonCommand(pub u32) {
    pub color: u32 @ 0..=23,
    pub raw_texture: bool @ 24,
    pub semi_transparent: bool @ 25,
    pub textured: bool @ 26,
    pub vertices_count: bool @ 27,
    pub gouraud: bool @ 28,
    pub command: u32 @ 29..=31,
}

Base count of extra data words is either 4 or 3 (will call the count vertices). 4 if vertices_count is set.

  • If gouraud is set, then vertices - 1 on top of that
  • If textured is set, then vertices

Basically: 

Gp0Command::PolygonPrimitive(cmd) => {
    let vertices = if cmd.vertices_count() { 4 } else { 3 };
    let mut base = vertices;

    // requires color for vertices 1..n (color 0 in cmd word)
    if cmd.gouraud() {
        base += vertices - 1;
    }

    // requires UV for each vertex (no vertex in cmd word)
    if cmd.textured() {
        base += vertices;
    }

    base
}

items.title: Rasterizer
items.text:
Given vertices v0, v1, v2, v3 to draw a rectangle/quad: 

v0 --- v1        Triangle 1: v0 -> v1 -> v2
|       |        Triangle 2: v1 -> v2 -> v3
|       |
v2 --- v3        Note: 0-indexed, see below

Quads are internally processed as two triangles, the first consisting of vertices 1,2,3, and the second of vertices 2,3,4. Source

fn rasterize_polygon(vertices: &[(i16, i16)], colors: &[u32], vram: &mut [u8]) {
    // fun stuff
}
  • If vertices.len() == 4 then we know we have a quad and must split it into 2 triangles
  • If not, then we operate on "Triangle 1" only
  • colors maps each coordinate with a color which can later be used for coloring and applying gradient
  • vram is just a reference to the internal VRAM storage

To get the coordinate/corner positions: 

let (x0, y0) = (vertices[0].0 as i32, vertices[0].1 as i32);
let (x1, y1) = (vertices[1].0 as i32, vertices[1].1 as i32);
let (x2, y2) = (vertices[2].0 as i32, vertices[2].1 as i32);

For optimization we can define a min/max (bounding box?) of the polygon so we can perform the math on this selection only: 

let min_x = x0.min(x1).min(x2).max(0);
let max_x = x0.max(x1).max(x2).min(VRAM_WIDTH as i32 - 1);
let min_y = y0.min(y1).min(y2).max(0);
let max_y = y0.max(y1).max(y2).min(VRAM_HEIGHT as i32 - 1);

  • min_x: The leftmost point of any corner
  • max_x: The rightmost point of any corner
  • min_y: The topmost point of any corner
  • max_y: The bottommost point of any corner

Now to fill a triangle we'll have to go through each point in the bounding box (?) and check whether this point is:

  • to the left of a line A to B
  • to the right of a line A to B
  • on top of a line A to B
fn edge_function(ax: i32, ay: i32, bx: i32, by: i32, px: i32, py: i32) -> i32 {
    (bx - ax) * (py - ay) - (by - ay) * (px - ax)
}

let area = edge_function(x0, y0, x1, y1, x2, y2); // if area == 0 -> straight line
let clockwise = area < 0;

let w0 = edge_function(x1, y1, x2, y2, x, y);
let w1 = edge_function(x2, y2, x0, y0, x, y);
let w2 = edge_function(x0, y0, x1, y1, x, y);

let inside = if clockwise {
    w0 <= 0 && w1 <= 0 && w2 <= 0
} else {
    w0 >= 0 && w1 >= 0 && w2 >= 0
};

// if inside == true -> pixel x,y is inside of triangle

To interpolate the colors: 

let r0 = (colors[0] & 0xFF) as i32;
let g0 = ((colors[0] >> 8) & 0xFF) as i32;
let b0 = ((colors[0] >> 16) & 0xFF) as i32;

let r1 = (colors[1] & 0xFF) as i32;
let g1 = ((colors[1] >> 8) & 0xFF) as i32;
let b1 = ((colors[1] >> 16) & 0xFF) as i32;

let r2 = (colors[2] & 0xFF) as i32;
let g2 = ((colors[2] >> 8) & 0xFF) as i32;
let b2 = ((colors[2] >> 16) & 0xFF) as i32;

// gouraud shading
let r = (r0 * w0 + r1 * w1 + r2 * w2) / area;
let g = (g0 * w0 + g1 * w1 + g2 * w2) / area;
let b = (b0 * w0 + b1 * w1 + b2 * w2) / area;

Since VRAM stores RGB values as RGB555 we'll have to modify them: 

let r5 = ((r >> 3) & 0x1F) as u16;
let g5 = ((g >> 3) & 0x1F) as u16;
let b5 = ((b >> 3) & 0x1F) as u16;
let pixel = (b5 << 10) | (g5 << 5) | r5;

items.title: Controller Input Issues
items.text:
Directional controls (up/down) on this screen might not work (even though other buttons work). This happens if SIO0 RX is sent for both ports at the same time (bit 13).

0     TX Enable (TXEN)      (0=Disable, 1=Enable)
1     DTR Output Level      (0=Off, 1=On)
2     RX Enable (RXEN)      (SIO1: 0=Disable, 1=Enable)  ;Disable also clears RXFIFO
                            (SIO0: 0=only receive when /CS low, 1=force receiving single byte)
3     SIO1 TX Output Level  (0=Normal, 1=Inverted, during Inactivity & Stop bits)
4     Acknowledge           (0=No change, 1=Reset SIO_STAT.Bits 3,4,5,9)      (W)
5     SIO1 RTS Output Level (0=Off, 1=On)
6     Reset                 (0=No change, 1=Reset most registers to zero) (W)
7     SIO1 unknown?         (read/write-able when FACTOR non-zero) (otherwise always zero)
8-9   RX Interrupt Mode     (0..3 = IRQ when RX FIFO contains 1,2,4,8 bytes)
10    TX Interrupt Enable   (0=Disable, 1=Enable) ;when SIO_STAT.0-or-2 ;Ready
11    RX Interrupt Enable   (0=Disable, 1=Enable) ;when N bytes in RX FIFO
12    DSR Interrupt Enable  (0=Disable, 1=Enable) ;when SIO_STAT.7  ;DSR high or /ACK low
13    SIO0 port select      (0=port 1, 1=port 2) (/CS pulled low when bit 1 set)
14-15 Not used              (always zero)

Based on bit 13 only respond for the selected port. In my case I ignore port 2 (returning 0xFF denotes absence).

match tx_byte {
    0x01 => {
        if self.control.port_number() == 2 {
            // If Port 2 is selected, no controller is present
            tracing::trace!(
                target: "psx_core::sio",
                tx = format!("{:02X}", tx_byte),
                "Port 2 selected - no device"
            );
            return 0xFF;
        }

        self.active_device = ActiveDevice::Controller;
    }
    0x81 => {
        self.active_device = ActiveDevice::MemoryCard;
    }
    _ => {}
}

When SIO0_CTRL is written, I also check whether the port number changed to 2 and reset the state machine if necessary: 

if matches!(self.active_device, ActiveDevice::None | ActiveDevice::Controller)
    && self.control.port_number() == 2
{
    self.reset_devices();
}

items.title: Fragmented Graphics
items.text:
Polygon commands must propagate their texpage to the global texpage.

// Update global texpage state from polygon's embedded texpage
// Texpage is in uvs[1] upper 16 bits (same location as for triangles/quads)
if uvs.len() > 1 {
    let texpage = ((uvs[1] >> 16) & 0xFFFF) as u16;

    // Extract texpage components (bits 0-8, 11 update global state)
    let texture_page_x_base = (texpage & 0xF) as u32;
    let texture_page_y_base_1 = ((texpage >> 4) & 0x1) != 0;
    let texture_page_colors = ((texpage >> 7) & 0x3) as u32;
    let texture_page_y_base_2 = ((texpage >> 11) & 0x1) != 0;

    // Update global GPU state (same as GP0(E1h) command)
    self.gp.gp1_status.set_texture_page_x_base(texture_page_x_base);
    self.gp.gp1_status.set_texture_page_y_base_1(texture_page_y_base_1);
    self.gp.gp1_status.set_texture_page_colors(texture_page_colors);
    self.gp.gp1_status.set_texture_page_y_base_2(texture_page_y_base_2);
}
